v.q: When is a synchronous call a better choice than publishing an event?
o: When the caller needs the answer right now, such as a balance query
When many services must react to a change later
When the receiver may be offline for hours
When the sender should never wait
v.w: Events suit work that can happen later and reactions by several parties. A query needing an immediate result is a synchronous call, protected by timeouts.

v.q: Which call is a good fit for events rather than a synchronous request?
o: Notifying other services after an account is opened
Reading a balance for the screen
Validating a card during checkout
Checking login credentials
v.w: When several services react later and the caller does not wait, an event decouples them.

v.q: What does an API gateway typically do?
o: Routes requests and handles authentication and rate limiting
Stores all business data for the services
Replaces every service-to-service call with events
Runs the business rules of each service
v.w: It keeps services private and simpler. Business logic does not belong in the gateway, or it becomes a bottleneck and a new monolith.

v.q: Which job does an API gateway NOT do?
o: Run the business rules
Route requests to services
Authenticate every caller
Apply rate limits per client
v.w: Business logic belongs in the services. The gateway handles edge concerns.

v.q: Why use a backend for frontend instead of one generic API?
o: Each client type gets responses shaped for it, owned by its own team
It removes the need for authentication
It makes all clients use the same payloads
It replaces the services behind it
v.w: A mobile BFF can return small combined responses while a web BFF returns richer data, without bending the shared services.

v.q: Which statement about a BFF is NOT true?
o: One BFF must serve every kind of client
A BFF is shaped for one client type
A mobile and a web BFF can differ
It reduces over-fetching
v.w: The idea is one backend per experience, such as web and mobile.

v.q: Which change to a JSON API is backward compatible?
o: Adding an optional field to a response
Renaming an existing field
Changing a number field to a string
Making an optional request field required
v.w: Old callers ignore fields they do not know, provided they are tolerant readers. Removals, renames and type changes break callers.

v.q: Which change is NOT backward compatible for existing clients?
o: Removing a field from a response
Adding an optional response field
Adding a new endpoint
Adding an optional request parameter
v.w: Clients may rely on a field, so removing it breaks them.

v.q: What does a consumer-driven contract test (Pact) give you?
o: The provider's build fails if a change would break what a consumer relies on
A full end-to-end test of all services at once
Automatic generation of the provider's business logic
A replacement for versioning and deprecation
v.w: Consumers record their expectations and the provider verifies them in CI, catching breaking changes before release.

v.q: Who writes the expectations in a consumer-driven contract test?
o: The consumer
The provider
The gateway
The database team
v.w: The consumer records what it needs, and the provider build verifies it.

v.q: When would you pick gRPC over REST?
o: For fast internal calls that need a strict typed contract and streaming
For public APIs that browsers call directly
When responses must be easy to cache by HTTP caches
When clients must read payloads in a text editor
v.w: gRPC generates typed code from a .proto file and uses compact Protobuf over HTTP/2. REST suits public APIs and browsers.

v.q: Which feature is a reason to choose gRPC?
o: Streaming with a typed contract
Direct browser calls
Easy HTTP caching
Human-readable payloads
v.w: gRPC uses Protocol Buffers over HTTP/2, which suits internal calls and streaming.

v.q: What is the standard format for returning HTTP API errors in Spring?
o: Problem Details (RFC 9457) with a type and status
A plain text message that includes the stack trace
An HTML error page shown to every client
A custom XML body that differs for each endpoint
v.w: Spring supports it as ProblemDetail. Add a machine-readable code and correlation id, and keep stack traces in the log.

v.q: Which header tells a client an error body uses Problem Details?
o: Content-Type: application/problem+json
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Type: text/html
Content-Type: application/xml
v.w: RFC 9457 defines the problem+json media type.

v.q: How does a caller find instances of a service on Kubernetes?
o: Through a Service with a stable DNS name
By hard-coding the current IP address of each pod
By asking the API gateway for pod addresses
By reading the node filesystem for addresses
v.w: The platform tracks ready pods behind the Service, so a separate registry is rarely needed.

v.q: Which Kubernetes object gives a stable name to a set of pods?
o: Service
Pod
ConfigMap
Node
v.w: A Service has a stable DNS name and IP and routes to the matching ready pods.
